mainTopic: Does יאוש make a thief the owner? And does a thief who sells before יאוש pay תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה? (רב נחמן and רב ששת)
overview: The גמרא asks whether יאוש (the owner giving up hope) makes a thief the owner of what he stole. It tests this with the thief's תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה for selling or slaughtering a stolen animal. If the thief already owned the animal, why would he pay a fine? Two proofs, from 'נשתרש בחטא' and from 'a sale that cannot be undone,' are pushed away. Next comes a ברייתא about a second thief, which seems to show that יאוש does not acquire. That is a difficulty for רב. רבא fixes the ברייתא's wording, רב פפא assigns its last case to בית שמאי, and רב זביד explains that the middle case has יאוש only once the animal is with the buyer. Then רב נחמן and רב ששת argue whether a thief who sells before יאוש pays the fine. רב ששת's proofs are pushed away. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to quote רבי אלעזר, who agrees with רב ששת; his statement comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The entrenched-in-sin proof: the sale must be after despair, so despair cannot give ownership
steps.stepSummary: The earlier source said the thief became 'entrenched in sin' by selling. That only makes sense if the sale works, which means after יאוש. But if יאוש made the animal his, why would he pay ארבעה וחמשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there any 'entrenchment' in a sale that does not work? So the sale must be after the owner's despair. But if despair makes the thief the owner, why does he pay four or five times? He is slaughtering his own animal and selling his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that יאוש does NOT make the thief the owner. It shows that the 'entrenched in sin' source must be talking about a sale after יאוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, a thief's sale does nothing legally, so he has not 'deepened' his sin. So the source must mean a sale after יאוש. But at that point, if יאוש קני, the animal is already his, and nobody pays a penalty for selling his own animal. So it looks like יאוש does not give ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: became rooted or entrenched (in sin)
the owner giving up hope of getting his item back
despair acquires, meaning it makes the thief the owner
if it enters your mind (if you think)
the fourfold or fivefold payment a thief pays for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of an argument. The words right before it asked, 'If you say the sale was before יאוש...' This line is the answer to that: before יאוש there is no real entrenchment.

phrases.english: Is there any 'entrenchment'?
phrases.notes: He means: before יאוש the sale doesn't work, so the thief didn't really sink deeper into the sin.

phrases.english: Rather, it must be after despair.
And if you think that despair acquires,
why does he pay the fourfold or fivefold payment?
He is slaughtering his own,
he is selling his own!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא נִשְׁתָּרֵשׁ? אֶלָּא לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that started before this section, from a source that used the phrase 'נשתרש בחטא'.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make the thief the owner (יאוש לא קני).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier source describing the selling thief as 'נשתרש בחטא', together with the ארבעה וחמשה penalty.

steps.title: Pushing away the proof: he is liable because he repeated the sin
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected using רבא's explanation. 'Entrenched' just means the thief sinned a second time by going through with a sale. That is true even before יאוש, when the sale does not legally work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: as רבא said, he pays because he repeated the sin. Here too, it is because he repeated the sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 1. 'Entrenched in sin' does not have to mean the sale legally worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed that 'entrenchment' needs a sale that actually works, which forced a time after יאוש. רבא's idea changes the meaning: the thief is liable because he did a second wrong act by selling, even if the sale is legally empty. So the source can be talking about before יאוש, and it tells us nothing about whether יאוש קני.

keyTerms.meaning: repeated the sin, did the wrong a second time
here too

phrases.english: They say: as Rava said:
because he repeated the sin;
here too, it is because he repeated the sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by reading 'נשתרש בחטא' differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the phrase 'נשתרש בחטא'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed that 'entrenchment' needs a sale that legally works. By רבא's reasoning, the liability comes from repeating the sinful act, so it can be before יאוש.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'entrenched in sin' proof fails. The thief can be liable for selling even when the sale has no legal effect, because he repeated his sin.

steps.title: A new proof: selling must be final, like slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק 'וטבחו או מכרו'. Just as slaughter cannot be undone, the selling that makes a thief pay must also be a sale that cannot be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'and slaughters it or sells it.' Just as slaughter cannot be undone, so too the selling must be one that cannot be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to prove that יאוש does not acquire. This step only brings the source; the next step will analyze it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares selling to slaughtering in the פסוק. A slaughtered animal can never be brought back, so the selling that counts must also be permanent. This sets up the question of when a thief's sale is permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: slaughtering
selling
cannot be undone or reversed

phrases.english: Come and hear: "and slaughters it or sells it";
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37

phrases.english: just as slaughtering cannot be undone,
so too selling must be one that cannot be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make the thief the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 21:37 that compares selling to slaughtering.

steps.title: Analyzing the new proof: an irreversible sale means after despair, so despair cannot give ownership
steps.stepSummary: A sale before יאוש is easy to undo, so the ברייתא must mean after יאוש. But if the thief owned the animal by then, he could not owe ארבעה וחמשה for his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this? If before despair, why can't it be undone? So it must be after despair. And if you think he owns it, why does he pay four or five times? He is slaughtering his own, he is selling his own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same logic as step 1 on the new ברייתא. It concludes that the thief does not own the animal after יאוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש a thief's sale has no legal power, so it can simply be cancelled, which does not fit 'cannot be undone.' That forces the case to be after יאוש. But then, if יאוש קני, the thief would be dealing with his own property and should not pay a penalty. So the proof points to יאוש לא קני.

keyTerms.meaning: when? (in what case?)
if you say
he acquired it

phrases.english: When? If you say before despair,
why can it not be undone?
phrases.notes: Before יאוש the thief's sale doesn't work, so the animal could just go back to the owner.

phrases.english: Rather, it must be after despair.
And if you think he acquired it,
why does he pay four or five times?
He is slaughtering his own,
he is selling his own!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ, אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ חוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 3, using the same logic as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make the thief the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that the sale must be one that 'cannot be undone,' which only fits a sale after יאוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a fresh attack on יאוש קני. It does not depend on the phrase 'נשתרש בחטא', so רבא's answer from step 2 does not obviously work here. The גמרא will need a new way to respond.

steps.title: The sale that 'cannot be undone' only leaves out a thirty-day sale
steps.stepSummary: The proof from 'וטבחו או מכרו' is rejected. The ברייתא only means to leave out a temporary sale, like a sale for thirty days, as רב נחמן explained in another place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said about another ברייתא: 'this leaves out someone who transferred it for thirty days.' Here too, it leaves out someone who transferred it for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 4. 'A sale that cannot be undone' does not mean a sale after יאוש. It just means a permanent sale, as opposed to a sale for a limited time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 thought 'cannot be undone' meant 'legally final,' which would only be true after יאוש. רב נחמן reads it differently: it only leaves out a sale that ends by itself, like one for thirty days. So a permanent sale made before יאוש still makes the thief pay ארבעה וחמשה, and nothing is proven about יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluding, leaving out
Transferred ownership
For thirty days, meaning a temporary transfer
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cannot be undone' here is not about whether the sale is legally valid. It is about whether the sale was meant to be permanent or only for a set time.

phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן said this about a different ברייתא. The גמרא borrows his answer for this case.

phrases.english: excluding one who transferred it for thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, פְּרָט לְשֶׁהִקְנָה לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: here too, it excludes one who transferred it for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 4 by reading 'cannot be undone' as 'not temporary.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the 'וטבחו או מכרו' ברייתא entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'cannot be undone' meant a legally binding sale after יאוש. It can simply mean a permanent sale rather than a thirty-day one.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about a second thief
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with three cases where a second thief steals the animal. These cases are: from the first thief, after the first thief sold it, and after the first thief slaughtered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: If someone stole an animal and another person came and stole it from him, the first thief pays double and the second pays only the value. If someone stole and sold it, and another came and stole it, the first pays four or five times and the second pays double. If someone stole and slaughtered it, and another came and stole it, the first pays four or five times and the second does not pay double, only the value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the question about יאוש. Here it only quotes the ברייתא; the actual argument comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases. In the first and third, the second thief pays only קרן, because he stole from a thief. In the middle case, after the animal was sold, the second thief pays כפל. That suggests the person he stole from is treated as a real owner, and the גמרא will build on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief pays
The principal, meaning just the value of what was stolen
The four- or five-times payment for stealing and then selling or slaughtering a sheep or ox

phrases.english: An objection was raised: If one stole, and another came and stole it from him,
the first pays double payment,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשֵּׁנִי אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶלָּא קֶרֶן בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: and the second pays only the principal.
If one stole and sold it, and another came and stole it,
the first pays four- or five-times payment,
and the second pays double payment.
If one stole and slaughtered it, and another came and stole it,
the first pays four- or five-times payment,
and the second does not pay double payment,
but only the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source to challenge the question about יאוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that יאוש makes the thief the owner (יאוש קני).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's payment rules, especially the middle case, show how the law treats the animal after the thief sells it. The גמרא will use that next.

steps.title: Focusing on the middle case: stole, sold, and then stolen again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the middle case of the ברייתא. There the first thief pays ארבעה וחמשה, and the second thief pays כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the middle clause teaches: If one stole and sold it, and another came and stole it, the first pays four or five times, and the second pays double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks out the middle case of the ברייתא to build its argument. This is setup: the inference itself comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facts sit side by side here. The second thief pays כפל, so the person he stole from (the buyer) seems to be a true owner. Yet the first thief still pays ארבעה וחמשה. The גמרא is about to ask what this means for whether יאוש gives ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches
The middle clause

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches in the middle clause:
If one stole and sold it, and another came and stole it,
the first pays four- or five-times payment,
and the second pays double payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא from Step 6 down to the one clause the argument depends on.
steps.raayaObject: Whether יאוש makes the stolen animal the thief's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The middle clause of the ברייתא: the second thief pays כפל, and the first thief pays ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: The middle case cannot be before the owner gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the sale in the middle case happened. It rules out before יאוש, because a change of hands alone, without יאוש, does not give anyone ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did this happen? If you say before יאוש, why does the second thief pay כפל? Does anyone hold that a change of hands without יאוש makes the new holder the owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the first thief sold the animal in the middle case. It shows that the sale could not have been before the owner gave up hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the buyer does not own the animal, because passing to a new person alone (שינוי רשות) does not give ownership. So the second thief would be stealing from a buyer who is not the owner. He should not owe that buyer כפל. Since the ברייתא says he does pay כפל, the case cannot be before יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say (the first option, soon to be rejected)
The owner giving up hope of getting his item back
The item passing from one person's possession to another's
The double payment a thief must pay

phrases.english: When?
phrases.notes: He means: when did the first thief sell the animal in the middle case of the ברייתא?

phrases.english: If we say before despair,
why does the second thief pay the double payment?
A change of possession without despair:
is there anyone who says that it acquires?
phrases.notes: This is a question that expects the answer no. Nobody holds that a change of hands alone makes the buyer the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the timing of the middle case pointed to in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the middle case of the ברייתא must be after יאוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that שינוי רשות without יאוש does not acquire, together with the ברייתא's ruling that the second thief pays כפל

steps.title: After the owner gave up hope, the first thief should not pay four or five
steps.stepSummary: So the sale must be after יאוש. But if יאוש made the thief the owner, he sold his own animal, so why does he pay ארבעה וחמשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it was after יאוש. And if you think יאוש acquires, why does he pay ארבעה וחמשה? He sold his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the sale cannot be before יאוש, the גמרא says it must be after יאוש. Then it shows that this causes a problem for the view that יאוש acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the first thief pays ארבעה וחמשה for selling the animal. If יאוש had already made him the owner, the sale would be of his own animal, and nobody pays a fine for selling what he owns. So the ברייתא seems to show that יאוש does not give the thief ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
If it enters your mind (if you think)
The four or five times payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen animal
His own

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: after despair.
And if it enters your mind that despair acquires,
why does he pay the fourfold or fivefold payment?
phrases.notes: This is talking about the first thief, the one who sold the animal.

phrases.english: It is his own that he sold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8: once the case must be after יאוש, it shows the problem for the view that יאוש acquires.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make a thief the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The middle case of the ברייתא, where the first thief pays ארבעה וחמשה after יאוש

steps.title: A second proof from the first case of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings more support from the first case: the first thief pays כפל, and the second thief pays only קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the first case teaches: if he stole, and another came and stole it from him, the first pays כפל, and the second pays only קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another proof by quoting the first case of the same ברייתא. This step sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the second thief steals straight from the first thief. The ruling is that the first thief pays כפל to the owner, and the second thief returns only the value of the animal. The גמרא will use this ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adding another point)
The first case of a ברייתא or משנה
The principal: just the value of what was stolen, with no fine

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which is taught in the first clause:
He stole, and another came and stole it from him:
the first pays the double payment,
and the second pays only the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second piece of evidence from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make a thief the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first case of the ברייתא of the second thief

steps.title: Why would the second thief pay only the principal?
steps.stepSummary: The whole ברייתא is after יאוש. If יאוש made the first thief the owner, the second thief should pay him כפל, not just קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we are dealing with after יאוש. And if you think יאוש acquires, why does the second thief pay only קרן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first case also works against the view that יאוש acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already showed that the ברייתא is talking about after יאוש. If יאוש made the first thief the owner, the second thief stole from a real owner and should pay him כפל. Since he pays only קרן, the first thief was not the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (pointing to something already established)
We are dealing with (this situation)

phrases.english: Now, we are dealing with after despair;
phrases.notes: We learned this from the middle case in steps 8 and 9, and the whole ברייתא is treated as talking about the same time.

phrases.english: and if it enters your mind that despair acquires,

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי אַמַּאי אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶלָּא קֶרֶן?
phrases.english: why does the second pay only the principal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the after-יאוש timing from step 9 to the first case quoted in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש does not make a thief the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that the second thief pays only קרן

steps.title: Despair does not acquire, which is a difficulty for רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that יאוש does not acquire, and this is a challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that יאוש does not acquire? And this is a difficulty for רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls the proofs together. It concludes that יאוש does not make a thief the owner, and that this is a difficulty for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases of the ברייתא make sense only if the thief stays a non-owner even after יאוש. This goes directly against רב, who holds that יאוש does acquire. The next steps answer this challenge: רבא, רב פפא and רב זביד each defend רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)
Despair does not acquire
A difficulty or challenge

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the second thief seems to show that even after יאוש, a thief is still not the owner. That is a strong challenge to רב, who holds יאוש קונה.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it
that despair does not acquire,
and it is a difficulty for Rav?
phrases.notes: רב is the one who holds that יאוש does make the thief the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ יֵאוּשׁ לָא קָנֵי, וְקַשְׁיָא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proofs in steps 9 and 11 and turns it against רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases of the ברייתא happen after יאוש. Yet the first thief pays ארבעה וחמשה for selling the animal, and the second thief pays the first thief only קרן. Both rulings show the first thief was not the owner, so יאוש does not acquire.

steps.title: רבא shows the ברייתא's wording cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how anyone could trust this ברייתא's wording. Its last case says a second thief who steals a slaughtered animal pays only קרן, yet everyone agrees that שינוי מעשה (slaughtering) makes the thief the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you really think this ברייתא is worded correctly? Look at its last case: a man stole an animal and slaughtered it, and then another man stole it from him. The first thief pays four or five times, and the second pays only the principal. But is there anyone who says that changing an item through an action does not make it yours?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is attacking the wording of the ברייתא that was just used against רב. He shows that one of its cases makes no sense as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is a שינוי מעשה, and everyone agrees that such a change makes the thief the owner. If the first thief owned the slaughtered animal, the second thief stole from an owner and should pay him כפל, not only קרן. So the ברייתא as printed cannot be accurate, and a faulty text cannot serve as a proof against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Accurate, properly worded (said of a text)
The last case or clause of a teaching
A physical change made to an item by an action, like slaughtering
The fourfold or fivefold payment for stealing and then slaughtering or selling a sheep or ox

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with the rule of the ברייתא's first two cases here. He is pointing out that its last case breaks a rule everyone agrees on, so the text itself must be off.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And do you really think this [ברייתא] is accurately worded?!
But look at what it teaches in the last case:
He stole and slaughtered, and another came and stole it from him –
the first pays the fourfold or fivefold payment,
and the second pays only the principal;
but is there anyone who says
that a change made by an action does not acquire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the proof against רב from Step 12 by showing the ברייתא's wording is unreliable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accuracy of the ברייתא's last case (stole and slaughtered, second thief pays only קרן).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone agrees שינוי מעשה acquires, so after slaughtering, the first thief owns the animal and the second thief should pay him כפל. A ruling of only קרן contradicts an agreed rule.

steps.title: Fixing the ברייתא: put it all before יאוש and swap the cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the whole ברייתא is before יאוש, and the rulings of the middle and last cases should be swapped. In the corrected sale case, the second thief pays only קרן, because a change of hands without יאוש does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole ברייתא is talking about before the owner gave up hope. Swap the last case with the middle case and the middle with the last, and read it like this: If he stole and sold, and another stole it from the buyer, the first thief pays four or five times, and the second pays only the principal, because a change of hands without the owner giving up hope does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his fix for the ברייתא. He moves the whole ברייתא to before יאוש and swaps the rulings of the middle and last cases, starting with the sale case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, a sale is only a שינוי רשות, and that alone does not make the buyer the owner. So the second thief stole from someone who is not the owner and pays only קרן. Once the whole ברייתא is before יאוש, it says nothing about what happens after יאוש, so it no longer challenges רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the owner gives up hope of getting the item back
Reverse, swap
The middle case of a teaching
A change of hands, when the item passes to another person

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the proof that יאוש does not acquire, so רב's view is safe again.

phrases.english: Rather, actually, the whole [ברייתא] is before the owner gave up hope,
and swap the last case with the middle case
and the middle case with the last case,
and say it like this:
He stole and sold, and another came and stole it –
phrases.notes: The second thief stole it from the buyer.

phrases.english: the first pays the fourfold or fivefold payment,
and the second pays only the principal –

phrases.aramaic: דְּשִׁינּוּי רְשׁוּת בְּלֹא יֵאוּשׁ לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: because a change of hands without the owner giving up hope does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's correction to the text he just showed was faulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the source: place the whole ברייתא before יאוש and swap the rulings of two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was after יאוש and showed that יאוש does not acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is entirely before יאוש. A sale then is only a שינוי רשות, which does not acquire, so the second thief pays only קרן.

steps.title: The corrected slaughter case: the second thief pays כפל
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the fix: in the slaughter case, the second thief pays כפל, because the first thief became the owner through שינוי מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole and slaughtered, and another came and stole it from him, the first thief pays four or five times, and the second pays double, because the first thief acquired it through the change he made by slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבא's corrected reading with the slaughter case, which now gets the ruling the sale case used to have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even before יאוש, slaughtering is a שינוי מעשה, and that makes the first thief the owner. So the second thief stole from an owner and pays him כפל. This fits the rule everyone agrees on, which was the problem רבא raised in Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered
The double payment a thief pays
He acquired it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the ברייתא is all before יאוש. A sale (שינוי רשות) does not acquire, but slaughtering (שינוי מעשה) does. So the ברייתא is no proof against רב.

phrases.english: He stole and slaughtered, and another came and stole it –
the first pays the fourfold or fivefold payment,
and the second pays the double payment;
because he acquired it through a change made by an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the swap begun in Step 14 by giving the corrected slaughter case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second half of the reworded ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the slaughter case the second thief pays only קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the slaughter case the second thief pays כפל, because slaughtering, a שינוי מעשה, made the first thief the owner.

steps.title: רב פפא: no swap, the last case follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says there is no need to swap the cases. The last case, where the second thief pays only קרן, follows בית שמאי, who hold that a changed item still belongs to its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Actually, do not swap the cases. The last case follows בית שמאי, who say that a changed item stays as it was, still belonging to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer to רבא's problem. He keeps the ברייתא's wording and explains the last case another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's problem was that nobody says שינוי מעשה fails to acquire. רב פפא answers that בית שמאי do say this: even after a change, the item still belongs to the original owner. So the first thief never owned the slaughtered animal, and the second thief pays only קרן, exactly as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not swap the cases
The school of שמאי, whose rulings often differ from בית הלל
A changed item stays as it was, meaning it still belongs to its owner

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying that the הלכה follows בית שמאי. He only says this one case in the ברייתא was taught according to their view, so its wording can stay.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Actually, do not swap [the cases];
the last case follows בית שמאי,
who say: a changed item stays in its place.
phrases.notes: "Stays in its place" means the item stays as it was legally, so it still belongs to the original owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's swap and offers a different way to solve the problem raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the case to a specific opinion (בית שמאי) instead of changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees שינוי מעשה acquires, so the last case must be reworded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last case follows בית שמאי, who hold that even after a change the item still belongs to its owner, so the second thief pays only קרן.

steps.title: Without the swap, the first and middle cases challenge רב
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is left as is, and it is talking about after יאוש, its first two cases contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first case and the middle case are a difficulty for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא's approach. If we don't swap the cases, the first two cases of the ברייתא seem to go against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that once the owner gives up (יאוש), the thief owns the item. In the first and middle cases, the first thief is still treated as a thief, not an owner. If the ברייתא is talking about after יאוש, that does not fit רב.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if we accept what was just said
The first case of a ברייתא or משנה
The middle case

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if we don't swap the cases, the way רב פפא said, and we read the ברייתא as talking about after יאוש.

phrases.english: the first case and the middle case are a difficulty for רב!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא וּמְצִיעֲתָא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's no-swap reading by showing it brings back the problem for רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that יאוש alone acquires, under רב פפא's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the swap, the ברייתא is about after יאוש. Yet the first thief is still treated as a non-owner, which goes against רב.

steps.title: The middle case: the owner gave up only once the item was with the buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the whole ברייתא is before יאוש. The middle case is where the owner gave up only after the sale, so the buyer acquires through יאוש plus שינוי רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Really, the whole ברייתא is talking about before יאוש. What case are we dealing with here? The owners gave up while the item was with the buyer, and had not given up while it was with the thief. So there is both יאוש and שינוי רשות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers the challenge by placing the whole ברייתא before יאוש. He then explains the middle case in a way that still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is easy: before יאוש, the thief does not own the item, so רב has no problem. In the middle case, the first thief sold before any יאוש, so he pays four or five times as a thief. The owner gave up only later, while the item was with the buyer. The buyer then owns it through יאוש plus a change of hands, so a second thief who steals from him pays כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeps an earlier idea and defends it)
What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)
Buyer
A change of possession, when the item passes to a new person

phrases.english: רב זביד said:
Really, the whole ברייתא is before the owner gave up,
and what case are we dealing with here?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the middle case, where the thief sold the animal and a second thief stole it from the buyer.

phrases.english: where the owners gave up while it was with the buyer
and had not given up while it was with the thief,
so there is both giving up and a change of possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: לְעוֹלָם כּוּלַּהּ לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Puts the ברייתא before יאוש, and limits the middle case to יאוש that happened only once the item was with the buyer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about after יאוש, so the first thief being treated as a non-owner goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything is before יאוש. In the middle case, יאוש came only after the sale, so the buyer acquires and the second thief pays כפל to him.

steps.title: Don't think both factors are needed: יאוש alone works for a thief
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד makes clear that his answer does not mean we need יאוש plus שינוי רשות. יאוש alone acquires for the thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: And don't say this is because we need both יאוש and שינוי רשות. Even יאוש alone also acquires for a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד heads off a wrong conclusion someone might draw from his answer. He confirms that he fully agrees with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the buyer acquires only because two factors came together, which would suggest that יאוש alone is not enough. רב זביד rejects that. Following רב, יאוש by itself is enough for a thief to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: And don't say (blocks a wrong conclusion)
By itself; alone
Acquires; becomes the owner

steps.confusionAlert: The case in the ברייתא happens to have both יאוש and שינוי רשות. That does not mean both are needed; יאוש alone is enough for the thief.

phrases.english: And don't say
that it is because we need both giving up and a change of possession,
rather, even with giving up alone
a thief also acquires;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּבָעֵינַן יֵאוּשׁ וְשִׁינּוּי רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the answer of step 18 so it does not undercut רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Heads off a wrong reading of the answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer acquires only because there were two factors, so יאוש alone would not be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: יאוש alone acquires for a thief, just as רב says.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא chose this case: it is the only way both thieves pay
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used a case with יאוש only at the buyer's stage because that is the only way both thieves end up paying fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just that you can't find a case where both of them pay, the first thief and the second thief, except this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד explains why the ברייתא picked such a specific case. This finishes his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner gave up before the sale, the first thief would already own the animal and would not pay four or five times. The ברייתא wanted a case where the first thief pays four or five times and the second thief pays כפל. That works only if יאוש comes after the sale, while the item is with the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: You find
Both of them
In this way; in this case

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד keeps רב's view: יאוש alone acquires for a thief. The ברייתא is all before יאוש, and its middle case has יאוש only once the item is with the buyer. It was chosen because that is the only way both thieves pay a fine.

phrases.english: it is just that you can't find
a case where both of them pay,
phrases.notes: The first thief pays four or five times, and the second thief pays double.

phrases.english: the first thief and the second thief,
except this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא chose the specific case described in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the choice of case by what the ברייתא wanted to show.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The choice of a case with both יאוש and שינוי רשות suggests that both are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was chosen only so that both thieves would pay fines.

steps.title: The dispute: selling before the owner gives up hope
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue whether a thief who sells a stolen animal before יאוש pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if a thief sells a stolen animal before the owner gives up hope, רב נחמן says he must pay the fine, and רב ששת says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת about a sale made before יאוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a sale that does not legally go through (because the owner has not yet given up hope) still counts as 'selling' for the four-or-fivefold fine. רב נחמן says yes (חייב). רב ששת says no (פטור).

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting the item back
Obligated to pay
Exempt, does not have to pay
The fine of four times (for a sheep) or five times (for an ox) paid by a thief who slaughters or sells it

steps.confusionAlert: Before יאוש, the sale does not legally transfer the animal to the buyer. The argument is whether such a sale that does not go through still triggers the fine.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who sells before despair —
phrases.notes: This is a thief selling an animal he stole, before the owner has given up hope of getting it back.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says: he is liable,
Rav Sheshet says: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the ברייתא and the opinion of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: a thief who sells before יאוש pays the fine. רב ששת: he is exempt.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason: the Torah just says 'sold'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the פסוק says 'and sold it,' and this thief did sell, so the timing does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says he is liable because the תורה says 'and sold it,' and this man did sell. It makes no difference whether this was before יאוש or after יאוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן holds the thief must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads the פסוק simply: the trigger is the act of selling. The תורה does not require that the sale actually works legally, so a sale before יאוש counts just like one after יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
He sold
There is no difference

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says he is liable —
'And sold it,' said the Merciful One,
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37

phrases.english: and this one did sell;
no difference if before despair,
no difference if after despair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב נחמן's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any act of selling counts for the fine, whether before or after יאוש.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason: the sale must work, like slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the sale must actually work, like slaughtering does. Before יאוש the sale does not work, so there is no fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת says he is exempt. The thief is only liable after יאוש, when his sale works. Before יאוש, when his sale does nothing, he is not liable. The selling must be like slaughtering, which really does something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב ששת holds the thief is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts selling next to slaughtering (טביחה). Slaughtering always has a real effect on the animal. So רב ששת says selling counts only when it also has a real effect, meaning a valid sale after יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: His actions were effective, they actually did something
Similar to, comparable to
Slaughtering
We require

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the core of the argument: is the fine about the act of selling itself (רב נחמן), or about a sale that really takes effect (רב ששת)?

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says he is exempt —
his liability is only after despair,
when his actions are effective;
phrases.notes: After יאוש the buyer really gets the animal, so the sale works.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ דְּלָא אַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו –
phrases.english: but before despair, when his actions are not effective —
he is not liable;
we require it to be similar to slaughter,
where his actions are effective.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב ששת's ruling, set against רב נחמן's reasoning in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling counts for the fine only when it works like slaughtering does, which means only after יאוש.

steps.title: רב ששת brings רבי עקיבא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says the four-or-fivefold fine is given because the thief 'became rooted in sin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: How do I know this? From a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, why did the תורה say that one who slaughtered or sold pays four or five times? Because he became rooted in sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a source to support his view. This step quotes the source, and the next step shows how he reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives a reason for the fine: by slaughtering or selling, the thief 'became rooted' (נשתרש) in his sin. רב ששת will argue that this rooting only happens when the sale really works.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
He became rooted (deeply set) in sin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לָהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say it?
As it was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
For what reason did the Torah say
that one who slaughtered or sold pays four or five times?
Because he became rooted in sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת backs up his reasoning from step 23 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that a sale before יאוש does not bring the fine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי עקיבא: the fine is because the thief נשתרש בחטא.

steps.title: Rooting in sin only happens after the owner gives up
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת argues that 'becoming rooted in sin' cannot happen before יאוש, so רבי עקיבא must mean a sale after יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this talking about? If you say before יאוש, is there any 'rooting'? Rather, isn't it after יאוש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב ששת's proof by asking when רבי עקיבא's case takes place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the sale does not go through, so the thief has not really sunk deeper into his sin. Only after יאוש, when the sale works and the animal is truly gone from the owner, can we say he became rooted. So the fine is only for a sale after יאוש, as רב ששת says.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say
Rather, is it not that... (introduces the conclusion the speaker wants)

phrases.english: When?
If you say before despair,
is there any rooting?
phrases.notes: A sale before יאוש does nothing, so the thief has not gone deeper into his sin.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not after despair?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from step 24 so that it supports רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: A sale before יאוש does not bring the fine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word נשתרש in רבי עקיבא's ברייתא only fits a sale after יאוש.

steps.title: רבא: it means he repeated the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof: רבי עקיבא means the thief 'repeated' his sin, and that is true even with a sale before יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It means because he repeated the sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת's proof by reading רבי עקיבא's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת read 'rooted in sin' as a sin that truly took effect. רבא says it simply means the thief sinned a second time: first he stole, then he sold. Even a sale that does not go through is a second sin, so the ברייתא fits רב נחמן too.

keyTerms.meaning: He repeated the sin, did it a second time

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: selling before יאוש still brings the fine, since the תורה just says 'sold.' רב ששת: only a sale that works (after יאוש), like slaughtering. רב ששת's proof from רבי עקיבא is pushed aside by רבא: 'rooted' can mean 'repeated' the sin.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Because he repeated the sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 24 and 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only rejects רב ששת's proof from the ברייתא, not his reasoning itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed נשתרש means a sin that took effect. It can also mean repeating the sin, which a sale before יאוש still is.

steps.title: A ברייתא compares selling to slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: just as slaughtering cannot be undone, the sale in the פסוק must also be one that cannot be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And slaughter it or sell it.' Just as slaughtering cannot be reversed, so too the selling must be a sale that cannot be reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to try to support רב ששת. This step quotes the source, and the next step will show how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the two words of the פסוק together. Slaughtering is permanent, because a dead animal cannot come back. So the sale that triggers the fine must also be a permanent, final sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering
Selling
That does not go back, meaning it cannot be undone

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And slaughter it or sell it";
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37

phrases.english: just as slaughter is something that cannot be undone,
so too the selling is one that cannot be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא pushed away the first proof from רבי עקיבא, the גמרא tries a second proof for רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that the fine applies only to a sale after יאוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing מכירה to טביחה: both must be something that cannot be undone

steps.title: A sale before יאוש can be undone, so the ברייתא must mean after יאוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when this sale happened. Before יאוש the sale is not valid and can be undone, so the ברייתא must be talking about after יאוש. That proves רב ששת's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did this sale happen? If before יאוש, why can't it be undone? It can, since the sale is not valid. So it must be after יאוש. We learn that the fine applies only after יאוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the ברייתא step by step and shows that it seems to prove רב ששת right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the owner gives up hope, the animal still belongs to him, so the thief's sale is not valid and the owner can take the animal back. That sale can be undone, so it does not match the ברייתא's rule. Only a sale after יאוש is final, so the fine must apply only then.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting his item back
If you say, which opens one possible option
And learn from it, which states the conclusion drawn from the source
Liability, meaning the obligation to pay

phrases.english: When did the sale happen? If you say before despair,
why can it not be undone?
phrases.notes: Before יאוש the sale is not valid, so the owner can easily take the animal back.

phrases.english: Rather, it must be after despair,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ חִיּוּבָא לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ הוּא!
phrases.english: and learn from this that the liability is only after despair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 27 proves רב ששת's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת: the fine applies only to a sale after יאוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that the sale must be one that cannot be undone, which is true only after יאוש

steps.title: רב נחמן: the ברייתא only excludes a temporary sale
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that 'cannot be undone' does not refer to יאוש. It only excludes a thief who sold the animal for a limited time, such as thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן explained the ברייתא: it comes to exclude one who transferred the animal for only thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes away the proof by reading the ברייתא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, the 'undoing' the ברייתא worries about is a sale built to end, where the animal goes back after thirty days. A permanent sale counts as one that 'cannot be undone,' even before יאוש. So the ברייתא says nothing about timing, and רב נחמן's view from step 22 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he gave his own reading of the source
To exclude, meaning this case is left out
Transferred ownership

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן is saying a sale before יאוש cannot be undone in practice. He is saying that 'cannot be undone' in the ברייתא means a permanent sale, not a temporary one.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman interpreted it:
to exclude one who transferred it to him for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step rejects the proof for רב ששת made in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of this ברייתא as proof for רב ששת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that 'cannot be undone' is about יאוש. It actually contrasts a permanent sale with a temporary one.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר also holds the fine applies only after יאוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רבי אלעזר also agrees with רב ששת, and begins to quote his statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר also holds that the liability is only after יאוש, as רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It says רבי אלעזר shares רב ששת's view, and his words will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about this ברייתא is over, and now the גמרא brings in another אמורא who agrees with רב ששת. The actual statement of רבי אלעזר, which shows his view, comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And also, which adds another opinion that agrees
Holds, meaning this is his opinion
His liability, meaning the thief's obligation to pay

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar also holds
that his liability is only after despair,
as Rabbi Elazar says:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר חִיּוּבֵיהּ לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the ברייתא was pushed away, the גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר also agrees with רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that the fine applies only after יאוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רבי אלעזר, which is quoted next
